spec_features.spec_quote: The model can end the loop by calling `finish`
spec_features.evidence: tools.py build_tools() defines a 'finish' tool; execute() dispatches it to ToolExecutor.finish() which sets self.finished=True (tools.py ~line 'self.finished = True'). loop.py:148-150 reads it: 'if self.executor.finished and self.allow_early_exit: transcript.ended_reason="finished_by_model"; break'. So a finish call actually stops the loop. allow_early_exit defaults True and is passed from config (experiment.yaml allow_early_exit: true).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool defined, dispatched, and honored as a stop (break). Note allow_early_exit could disable it, but default is true and config enables it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the model emits a 'give_up' / final answer tool, whether to end early.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop also caps at `max_turns` and a wall-clock limit
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:102 'for turn in range(self.max_turns):' with loop.py:160 'else: transcript.ended_reason="max_turns"' — the for-range bounds iterations. Wall-clock: loop.py:103-105 'if time.time()-transcript.started_at > self.max_seconds: transcript.ended_reason="timeout"; break'. Both checked each turn and actually break/stop. Values come from config (max_turns:40, max_seconds:1800).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are compared and acted on (break / loop termination). Genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard stop on wall-clock per rollout, seconds. Safety, not scientific.
